import statistics

# Data from 1979 (treasury_bulletin_1980_03_page_88.txt)
# Fourth column group (after 1970, 1973, 1976 header groups)
treasury_1979 = [8.43, 8.43, 8.45, 8.44, 8.55, 8.32, 8.35, 8.42, 8.68, 9.44, 9.80, 9.58]
corp_1979 = [9.47, 9.52, 9.65, 9.69, 9.82, 9.51, 9.47, 9.57, 9.87, 11.17, 11.52, 11.30]

# Data from 1984 (treasury_bulletin_1985_03_page_48.txt)
# Fourth column group (after 1973, 1976, 1981 header groups)
treasury_1984 = [11.82, 12.00, 12.45, 12.65, 13.43, 13.54, 13.36, 12.71, 12.42, 12.04, 11.66, 11.64]
corp_1984 = [12.65, 12.80, 13.36, 13.64, 14.41, 14.49, 14.25, 13.54, 13.37, 13.02, 12.40, 12.47]

print("1979 data points:", len(treasury_1979), len(corp_1979))
print("1984 data points:", len(treasury_1984), len(corp_1984))

# Function to calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
def pearson_correlation(x, y):
    n = len(x)
    mean_x = sum(x) / n
    mean_y = sum(y) / n
    
    # Calculate deviations
    dx = [xi - mean_x for xi in x]
    dy = [yi - mean_y for yi in y]
    
    # Calculate covariance and standard deviations
    cov = sum(dx[i] * dy[i] for i in range(n))
    std_x = (sum(d**2 for d in dx) ** 0.5)
    std_y = (sum(d**2 for d in dy) ** 0.5)
    
    return cov / (std_x * std_y)

# Calculate correlations
corr_1979 = pearson_correlation(treasury_1979, corp_1979)
corr_1984 = pearson_correlation(treasury_1984, corp_1984)

print(f"\n1979 Pearson correlation: {corr_1979}")
print(f"1984 Pearson correlation: {corr_1984}")

# Calculate absolute difference
abs_diff = abs(corr_1979 - corr_1984)
print(f"\nAbsolute difference: {abs_diff}")
print(f"Rounded to 4 decimal places: {round(abs_diff, 4)}")
